chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
Cutting the head of the deceased is harsher (more severe) than cutting the head of the living.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling on cutting the head of a deceased person compared to a living one?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that severing the head of a deceased person is more severe than doing so to a living one, a ruling derived from the principle that the body of the deceased retains the sanctity of the soul (ruh) even after death. This distinction underscores the continuity of bodily honor in Shia jurisprudence, where dismemberment of the dead is viewed as a greater violation of the person's integrity than similar acts against the living.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel, from someone else from our companions, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘Cutting-off of the head of the deceased is harsher than cutting a head of the living’.
